security_audit.summary: The audit confirms real external command, secret-handling, and screen-recording upload risks in the ScreenCI workflow. Most Ruby backtick detections are Markdown false positives, but record commands upload captured screens and SCREENCI_SECRET is written to screenci/.env. SKILL.md also contains suspicious XML-like closing tags that should be removed.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation immediately before npx screenci record, and state that the result uploads to ScreenCI.
Avoid passing secrets as command arguments. Prefer protected local environment setup and verify .env files are excluded from version control.
Pin ScreenCI CLI versions instead of using latest and document what each command changes before it runs.
Remove the stray </content> and </invoke> lines from SKILL.md to avoid prompt boundary confusion.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable walkthrough videos that match real application flows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through ScreenCI scripts, narration, testing, and recording.
actual_capabilities: Creates and edits .screenci.ts recording scripts under recordings/.
Defines ScreenCI videos with narration cues and voice render options.
Uses Playwright locators with ScreenCI zoom, hide, overlay, and audio helpers.
Runs npx screenci test before final recording.
Runs npx screenci record to create recording.mp4, data.json, and an uploaded result URL.
Explains optional SCREENCI_SECRET setup and anonymous trial uploads.
limitations: Requires an existing ScreenCI project and Node.js 18 or newer.
Successful recordings upload to ScreenCI, so sensitive screens need review first.
Needs reliable selectors, URL context, or source context for best results.
Anonymous and free-tier renders may include a ScreenCI watermark.

best_practices: Run ScreenCI tests until selectors, narration, and page flow pass before recording.
Use demo accounts and scrub sensitive data before any record command.
Keep narration purposeful and use zoom only when it improves viewer focus.
anti_patterns: Do not record production credentials, private customer data, or internal dashboards.
Do not run record before the script passes repeatable tests.
Do not delete an existing screenci directory to force a new initialization.

faq.question: Does this skill require a ScreenCI account?
faq.answer: No. Recording can use an anonymous trial session, but it still uploads the result to ScreenCI.

faq.question: Will recordings be uploaded?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented record workflow uploads successful recordings and returns a ScreenCI result link.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it initialize a new ScreenCI project?
faq.answer: The references explain initialization, but the main workflow expects an already initialized project.

faq.question: What files does it edit?
faq.answer: It mainly edits .screenci.ts files, screenci.config.ts, and related recording assets.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use SCREENCI_SECRET only with user consent, keep it out of logs, and protect any local .env file.
